title: Marseilles - The Arrival
recap: Marseilles, 24 February 1815. The Pharaon comes into port with young Edmond Dantès, the mate, in command: Captain Leclere died of brain fever on the voyage. Danglars, the supercargo, complains to the shipowner, Morrel, that Edmond wasted time at Elba; Edmond explains he was carrying out the dying captain’s order to take a packet to Marshal Bertrand, and that he met the emperor there. Morrel means to make him captain and gives him leave to marry Mercédès and then go to Paris, while Danglars tells Morrel he saw the captain give Edmond a letter as well.

title: Father and Son
recap: Edmond hurries home and finds his father weak and hungry: while Edmond was away, their neighbour Caderousse made the old man repay a debt of Edmond’s, leaving him sixty francs to live on for three months. Caderousse calls to congratulate Edmond, eyes his money and hints that Mercédès has other admirers. Edmond leaves to see her at the Catalans. Caderousse then tells Danglars that she is often seen with a Catalan cousin, and the two settle at La Réserve to wait for news.

title: The Catalans
recap: In the Catalan village outside Marseilles, Fernand begs his cousin Mercédès to marry him; she refuses, saying she loves Edmond. Edmond arrives, and Mercédès makes Fernand shake his hand before he rushes out. Danglars and Caderousse, drinking in the arbour at La Réserve, call him over and needle him while Caderousse gets drunk. Edmond and Mercédès pass by; Edmond says the wedding will be tomorrow or the next day and that he must then go to Paris on Captain Leclere’s last errand, which gives Danglars an idea.

title: Conspiracy
recap: In the arbour, Danglars draws out Fernand’s jealousy while Caderousse gets drunk. Since Mercédès has sworn to kill herself if Edmond dies, Danglars suggests prison instead, and with his left hand writes an anonymous letter to the king’s attorney: Edmond took a letter from Murat to Napoleon on Elba and now carries one from Napoleon to the Bonapartist committee in Paris. When Caderousse calls it a shame, Danglars crumples it and throws it into a corner, as if in jest. Leading Caderousse back towards Marseilles, he looks back and sees Fernand pick up the letter and hurry off.

title: The Marriage Feast
recap: At La Réserve the betrothal feast becomes a wedding day: thanks to Morrel, Edmond and Mercédès are to marry at the city hall that afternoon, and Edmond leaves for Paris next morning. As the party sets off, a magistrate and soldiers arrest Edmond and take him away. Morrel returns with news that he is charged with being a Bonapartist agent; Caderousse wants to speak up about the letter, but Danglars frightens him into silence. Morrel puts Danglars in temporary command of the Pharaon.

title: The Deputy Procureur du Roi
recap: At about the same hour, in a mansion in Marseilles, Villefort celebrates his betrothal to Renée de Saint-Méran among royalist guests. Renée’s mother raises his father’s revolutionary past, and Villefort says he has dropped his father’s name and is a firm royalist. Called away from the table, he returns to read out an anonymous letter accusing Edmond Dantès of carrying letters for the Bonapartists. Edmond is being held at his house, and Villefort leaves to deal with him.

title: The Examination
recap: Morrel stops Villefort in the street to plead for Edmond and gets a cold reply. Villefort questions Edmond, finds him honest, shows him the anonymous letter (Edmond does not know the writing) and is about to free him when he learns the letter from Elba is addressed to M. Noirtier in Paris: his own father. He burns it, makes Edmond swear to deny it ever existed, and has him held. Alone, he decides the letter that nearly ruined him will make his fortune.

title: The Château d’If
recap: That night Edmond is taken by carriage and boat out past the Catalans, where he sees a light in Mercédès’s window. Only when the rock is in sight does a gendarme tell him he is bound for the Château d’If; he tries to throw himself overboard and is held down at gunpoint. Locked in a cell, he asks to see the governor, and when the jailer will not carry word to Mercédès he threatens him with a stool and is moved down to a dungeon.

title: The Evening of the Betrothal
recap: Villefort tells the Marquis de Saint-Méran to sell his government stock at once and gets a letter that will take him straight to the king in Paris, so that no one else can claim the credit for his discovery. At his door Mercédès begs for news of Edmond; he calls Edmond a great criminal and turns her away, then feels remorse for the first time but leaves anyway. Fernand stays beside Mercédès all night, Morrel’s appeals for Edmond are refused everywhere, Caderousse drinks alone and Danglars sleeps soundly. Old Dantès waits anxiously for news.

title: The King’s Closet at the Tuileries
recap: At the Tuileries on 3 March, Louis XVIII annotates his Horace and teases the Duc de Blacas about his fears of a Bonapartist rising, while the minister of police, Baron Dandré, reports Napoleon idle and failing on Elba. Blacas presents Villefort, and the king recalls that he is Noirtier’s son. Villefort warns that Napoleon is arming three ships and may already have left Elba. The king is shaken but still confident when Dandré reappears at the door, pale and trembling.

title: The Corsican Ogre
recap: Dandré tells the king that Napoleon left Elba on 26 February and has landed near Antibes. The king scorns his minister and praises Villefort, whose warning came first; Villefort tactfully shields Dandré and is given the king’s own Legion of Honour cross. The police report that General Quesnel, who vanished after leaving a Bonapartist club, was murdered, and describe the man who arranged to meet him. Back at his hotel, Villefort has an unannounced visitor who fits that description: his father.

title: Father and Son
recap: Villefort tells Noirtier he burnt the letter from Elba and warns that the police are on the trail of the Bonapartist club in the Rue Saint-Jacques, of which Noirtier is vice-president; Noirtier coolly gives his own version of General Quesnel’s visit there and predicts Napoleon will reach Paris within weeks. When Villefort repeats the police description, Noirtier shaves off his whiskers, puts on his son’s clothes and walks out past the watchers in the street. Villefort gets rid of the cast-off clothes and hurries back to Marseilles.

title: The Hundred Days
recap: Napoleon retakes the throne for the Hundred Days, then loses it at Waterloo. Morrel asks Villefort to free Edmond; Villefort dictates a petition that paints Edmond as an active Bonapartist, then keeps it instead of sending it, and Edmond stays forgotten in his dungeon. After Waterloo Villefort moves to Toulouse and marries Renée. Danglars leaves for Madrid, Fernand and Caderousse are called up, and Old Dantès dies in Mercédès’s arms.

title: The Two Prisoners
recap: On 30 July 1816 an inspector of prisons tours the dungeons of the Château d’If. Edmond begs him for a trial and is promised an inquiry, but the register calls him a violent Bonapartist, in a note added in a different hand, and the inspector writes “Nothing to be done.” The inspector also visits No. 27, the Abbé Faria, thought mad because he offers millions for his freedom. A year later the governor is replaced, and Edmond becomes simply number 34.

title: Number 34 and Number 27
recap: Years pass in solitude. Edmond turns from prayer to rage to despair and starts starving himself, until he hears someone scraping inside the wall. He digs towards the sound with a broken jug and a saucepan handle, and a voice answers: No. 27, a prisoner since 1811, whose escape tunnel meant for the sea has come out in the wrong place. The next morning the man climbs up through the floor into Edmond’s cell.

title: A Learned Italian
recap: Faria checks Edmond’s cell, finds every way out blocked and gives up hope of escape. He introduces himself as the Abbé Faria, jailed since 1811 for plotting to unite Italy, and admits he is the prisoner thought mad. Edmond, inspired by him, proposes breaking into the gallery and killing the sentry, but Faria will not take a life and says they must wait for a chance. He describes the pens, ink and linen book he has made, and leads Edmond back through the tunnel to see them.

title: The Abbé’s Chamber
recap: In his cell Faria shows Edmond his book written on linen, his pens, ink, lamp and rope ladder. Questioning Edmond, he shows that Danglars wrote the denunciation, that Fernand was with him, and that Villefort buried the case because the letter was addressed to his own father, Noirtier; Edmond resolves on revenge. Faria teaches him science, history and languages, and over fifteen months they dig a tunnel under the sentry’s gallery. Just as it is finished, a seizure paralyses Faria’s right arm and leg; he cannot escape, and Edmond swears never to leave him.

title: The Treasure
recap: Faria shows Edmond a half-burnt paper and says half his treasure is Edmond’s; Edmond fears he has relapsed into madness. Faria tells the story: in 1498 Pope Alexander VI and Cæsar Borgia poisoned Cardinal Spada for his wealth, but his fortune was never found. Centuries later Faria, secretary to the last Count of Spada, inherited the family breviary and found in it the cardinal’s will, written in invisible ink, saying the treasure lies in the caves of the small island of Monte Cristo. He promises Edmond half, or all of it if he dies, and calls him his son.

title: The Third Attack
recap: Faria makes Edmond learn the treasure letter by heart and advises him how to recover the treasure; Edmond draws him a plan of Monte Cristo, which he has sailed past. One night a third seizure strikes. Edmond gives him all the remaining drug, but Faria dies, telling him with his last words not to forget Monte Cristo. Hidden in the passage, Edmond hears the governor and the doctor confirm the death with a hot iron and have the body put in a sack to be buried that evening.

title: The Cemetery of the Château d’If
recap: Alone with Faria’s body, Edmond thinks of dying, then resolves to live and punish those who wronged him. He moves the body to his own bed and sews himself into the burial sack, planning to dig his way out of the grave. Instead the bearers tie a thirty-six-pound shot to his feet and throw him from the rocks into the sea, which is the cemetery of the Château d’If.
